tx.t: In this lecture I will describe how honeybees live and why they matter so much to farmers. A single summer hive can contain up to sixty thousand bees, but only one queen.

The queen can lay as many as two thousand eggs in one day. Worker bees live for only about six weeks in summer, and they spend their lives doing different jobs, from cleaning the hive to collecting nectar.

In its whole life, one worker produces only about one-twelfth of a teaspoon of honey. Bees tell each other where food is by dancing. The angle of the dance shows the direction, and its length shows the distance.
Many crops, such as almonds and apples, depend on bees to carry pollen from flower to flower.

What does the length of the dance show?

Then things changed, because the railway came and brought cheaper goods from the cities. As a result, many small traders went out of business.

By twenty ten, the number had risen to three hundred and seventy-eight pairs, which shows that careful management can work.

tx.t: Today I would like to outline what glaciers are, and why they matter for sea level. Glaciers cover about ten per cent of the world's land area.
Together, glaciers and ice sheets store about two thirds of the world's fresh water. A glacier forms when snow builds up for many years and is pressed into dense ice.
Since nineteen hundred, the global sea level has risen by about twenty centimetres. This rise is caused partly by melting ice and partly because warm water takes up more space.

On average, the students studied for four hours a day. However, only sixty-five per cent of them used any planned method.
The students who used the method of sleeping at least eight hours made fewer mistakes in the test. The researchers concluded that how you study may matter more than how long you study.

tx.t: Today I would like to talk about the Great Barrier Reef, the largest coral reef system in the world. It stretches for roughly two thousand three hundred kilometres.
It is not one reef but a network of nearly three thousand individual reefs. More than one thousand five hundred species of fish live there, together with many kinds of turtles and sharks.
It was added to the UNESCO World Heritage list in nineteen eighty-one. Warm water causes corals to expel the algae that feed them, which turns them white. This is called bleaching.
Scientists say that rising sea temperatures are the greatest long-term threat to the reef.

tx.t: Today I would like to describe a bike-sharing scheme in the town of Ashby. It began in twenty fifteen with eight hundred and two bikes, placed at stations around the centre.
Use grew quickly. Within three years the number of journeys had risen by twenty per cent, and on a busy day there were more than sixteen thousand trips.
The scheme soon met a serious problem: empty stations at rush hour. The council solved it with a mobile app that shows where bikes are available.
Today, a ride costs two pounds twenty-five for the first half hour, and the first fifteen minutes are free for residents.

tx.t: Today I will outline how solar power works and why its use is growing. Solar panels contain photovoltaic cells, which turn sunlight directly into electricity.
Most cells are made of silicon, the second most common element in the Earth's crust. The first practical silicon solar cell was made at Bell Laboratories in nineteen fifty-four.
A typical modern panel converts about twenty per cent of the sunlight that hits it into electricity. Over the last decade the cost of panels has fallen by about ninety per cent.
A panel usually works for about twenty-five years, although its output slowly declines.

The students who used the method of testing themselves instead of rereading scored higher in the final exam. The researchers concluded that how you study may matter more than how long you study.
